# Notes of this project for coding agents

Player Switch for Autodarts: Chrome extension for a shared Autodarts display: everyone plays under their own account and a tap on a tile switches players. Sessions are parked and kept fresh, so nobody signs in again; an optional remembered password signs an account back in by itself. Everything stays on the computer.

This file belongs to the project: the blueprint wrote it once, and its updates leave it alone. It adds to `AGENTS.md` what a coding agent needs to know about this project alone, such as its architecture, the commands of its own checks and what to watch for in its tests.

## Where things are

- The package is in `src/`, its metadata and version in `package.json`. Every line that ships is TypeScript there, built into `extension/lib/`, which git ignores: the service worker (`worker.ts`, which `background.ts` starts on the real `chrome` through the typed port `ChromeApi`), the content script (`content.ts`, a classic script that imports and exports nothing, since a content script can't be a module), the types of every message (`messages.ts`), what the pages decide (`popup-model.ts`, `options-model.ts`) and the pages themselves (`pages/`). `extension/` holds only the manifest, the HTML, the styles, the icons and the texts; never add JavaScript there. [docs/development.md](../docs/development.md#how-the-code-is-laid-out) has the layout.
- `README.md` documents installation, configuration and use, `docs/` holds the pages of the website, and `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of every release.
- The tests are in `test/`; `scripts/check.sh` runs every check.
- The end-to-end tests are in `test/e2e/`: `npm run e2e` runs the built extension in Playwright's Chromium against the fake Autodarts of `test/e2e/fake/`, and the browser reaches no other host; the workflow E2E runs them for every pull request that changes the extension, `src/` or the tests (required check `e2e`). A change of the popup, the switcher, the content script, the service worker or the manifest comes with a test there when a player would notice it, beside its unit test (`test/worker.test.ts` on the fake browser of `test/browser.ts`, `test/content.test.ts` beside a page of happy-dom); the fake fails every test that sends a refresh token twice. [docs/development.md](../docs/development.md#end-to-end-tests) has the details.
- What the extension relies on at Autodarts, the key of the session, the sign-in service and its client, is in `src/autodarts.ts`, with copies in `src/content.ts`, the manifest and the fake of `test/e2e/fake/`. The workflow Upstream checks it against the real Autodarts every morning (`scripts/upstream-contract.ts`, with made-up data only) and runs the end-to-end tests in Chrome for Testing Beta every morning too; a test fails when a copy no longer matches. Change them together, and never send a real account or token in a test. [docs/development.md](../docs/development.md#what-autodarts-and-the-next-chrome-change) has the details.
- The pictures of the extension in the README, on the website and in the store (`docs/images/*.png`, `*.gif` beside the diagrams, and `store/images/`) come from `bash scripts/screenshots.sh`, with Docker: `test/harness/` shows the real popup and switcher with a stand-in for Chrome and made-up accounts. The pictures of the store come in every language of `extension/_locales/`, with the words around the extension from `store/pictures.<code>.json`. Never edit a picture by hand; change the extension, these texts or the harness and render again, or leave it to the screenshot bot. [docs/development.md](../docs/development.md#pictures) has the details.
- The zip of a release comes from `bash scripts/package-extension.sh`, which `scripts/release-assets.sh` runs in the isolated build, and the store gets exactly that file: `.github/workflows/publish-store.yml` builds nothing and runs no npm (decision 0013). The same commit has to make the same bytes on every computer, and a new kind of file in `extension/` goes into `SHIPS` or `STAYS_OUT` of `scripts/package-extension.ts`, or the build fails. [docs/releases.md](../docs/releases.md#the-zip-of-a-release) has the details.
- One package runs in Chrome, Edge and Firefox (decision 0012): the manifest names `background.js` both as `service_worker` and in `scripts`, and the id of the add-on and the data that it sends in `browser_specific_settings.gecko`. `scripts/check-firefox.mjs` lints `extension/` with addons-linter in `scripts/check-project.sh`; the end-to-end tests run in Chromium alone, so code that differs between the browsers, such as the address of the extension's pages (`moz-extension://<uuid>/` in Firefox), gets a unit test with both, and a release is checked in Firefox by hand ([docs/development.md](../docs/development.md#firefox-and-edge)).
